question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched position within the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced by the abolition of term limits and ongoing personnel purges that have sidelined potential rivals, underpins trader expectations he will remain paramount leader through at least the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027. Recent developments, including the August 2026 Beidaihe conclave, July emphasis on party discipline and “Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building,” and appointments of loyal figures like Cai Qi, signal continuity rather than transition. No public signals of resignation or health-driven withdrawal have emerged, and succession planning remains deferred. While a sudden medical event or unforeseen elite fracture could theoretically alter the timeline, the absence of credible near-term catalysts aligns with the market’s 95 percent-plus consensus that removal before 2027 is improbable.

eventMetadata.context_description: Following the 2024 election loss, Democrats face an open 2028 nomination with no incumbent or clear frontrunner, prompting early positioning by governors, senators, and progressive figures ahead of the DNC's newly approved calendar that elevates South Carolina on January 22, 2028, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, and Virginia. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez leads trader consensus at 22.7 percent amid progressive momentum, while Gavin Newsom and Jon Ossoff tie at 14.8 percent, reflecting regional and establishment appeal; Kamala Harris trails at 7.4 percent despite some polling strength. The crowded field of over twenty potential candidates keeps probabilities tight, with separation likely hinging on 2026 midterm results, fundraising, debate performances, and coalition-building among diverse voter blocs.
